Letter from the Chairman





                            Dear Shareholders,       " It is my pleasure to present Hastings
                                         Technology Metals’ Annual Report for
                                            the financial year ended 30 June 2026.
               "



           A year of transition and repositioning

                The year was marked by significant changes to the Group’s asset portfolio
                and development strategy.

                The unincorporated joint venture with Wyloo over the Yangibana Rare
                   Earths and Niobium Project was completed in September 2025, with
                   Hastings retaining a 40% participating interest and Wyloo holding the
                  remaining 60% interest and was appointed manager and operator. This

Yangibana Joint Venture

Completion of the Yangibana unincorporated joint venture on 21 September 2025 followed after
shareholder approval on 30 July 2025. As a result, Wyloo Gascoyne Pty Ltd holds a 60% participating
interest and acts as manager and operator, while Hastings retains a 40% participating interest.

At completion, the remaining Wyloo Exchangeable Notes were cancelled and the final cash
settlement of $7.363 million was paid. The settlement was principally funded from the sale of
the Group’s remaining investment in Neo Performance Materials Inc. for approximately $14.6
million. Completion removed the Exchangeable Note liability from the Group’s balance sheet
and reduced Hastings’ direct funding exposure to Yangibana from 100% to 40%.

Activity following completion focused on integrating the Hastings and Wyloo technical teams,
reviewing the life-of-mine plan and engineering packages, and completing an updated Definitive
Feasibility Study for Yangibana Stage 1.

The updated study, released after year end on 13 July 2026, reported an estimated initial Stage
1 capital requirement of $333.4 million on a 100% Project basis, a pre-tax net present value at
an 8% discount rate of approximately $649 million and an ungeared pre-tax internal rate of
return of 34%. The study supports a 19-year mine life based entirely on Proved and Probable
Ore Reserves. No Final Investment Decision has been made and development remains subject
to securing the required funding.

Wyloo subsequently advised that, as part of its broader capital allocation priorities, it intended
to divest its 60% participating interest in the Yangibana Project. A sale process commenced
in April 2026 and attracted interest from a number of prospective investors. The process has
introduced some uncertainty around the timing of the next phase of Project development. As at
the date of this letter, Wyloo's sale process remains ongoing, and Hastings continues to engage
constructively while considering the implications for the Project and the Company's retained
40% interest.

Last October, the joint venture also entered into a non-binding Heads of Agreement with
Ucore Rare Metals Inc. to evaluate a potential long-term offtake arrangement for Yangibana
concentrate and hydrometallurgical processing options in the United States. Any definitive
arrangement remains subject to further technical and commercial evaluation and agreement
between the parties.

2  Remuneration Governance and Principles

2.1 Remuneration principles

The Board seeks to establish remuneration arrangements that are appropriate for the responsibilities and experience
of each KMP and the Company's circumstances. The remuneration framework is intended to:

     attract and retain appropriately experienced executives and Directors;
    provide fixed remuneration that is competitive but responsible;
     link executive reward to the achievement of strategic, operational and financial objectives;
     align longer-term executive outcomes with shareholder interests; and
    support sound risk management and conduct consistent with the Company's values.

Executive remuneration is considered separately from Non-Executive Director remuneration. Executive remuneration
may include fixed and performance-related components, whereas Non-Executive Directors generally receive fixed fees
reflecting their responsibilities and time commitments.

    During the year ended 30 June 2026, the Group completed the acquisition and subsequent disposal of the Whiteheads

   On 21 August 2025, the Group acquired 100% of the shares in Great Western Gold Pty Ltd, which held a 75% joint venture
     interest in the Whiteheads Gold Project. The acquisition was assessed as an asset acquisition rather than a business
    combination. Total consideration was $1,270,000, comprising 3,000,000 Hastings ordinary shares with a fair value of

NOTE 11: ASSETS AND LIABILITIES HELD FOR SALE

At 30 June 2025, a 60% interest in the Yangibana Project was classified as a disposal group held for sale in connection
with the Wyloo transaction, which completed on 21 September 2025. Accordingly, there were no assets or liabilities
classified as held for sale at 30 June 2026.

Transaction with Wyloo

On 15 February 2025, the Group executed a Share Purchase Agreement and related Set-off and Amendment Deed
with Wyloo Consolidated Investments Pty Ltd and its related entities (“Wyloo”). The transaction followed the transfer of
8,350,311 Neo Performance Materials Inc. shares to Wyloo on 15 February 2025 in partial settlement of the Exchangeable
Notes.

On 15 May 2025, the Group and Wyloo entered into a Transaction Agreement together with a Deed of Termination,
Release and Standstill in respect of the Exchangeable Notes. Under these agreements, Wyloo agreed to acquire a 60%
participating interest in the Yangibana Project, with the Group retaining a 40% participating interest. No further interest
accrued on the Exchangeable Notes from 15 February 2025.

On 21 September 2025, the Group and Wyloo executed the Joint Venture Agreement and completed the transaction.

Key commercial terms of the transaction included:

   Wyloo acquired a 60% participating interest in the Yangibana Project and was appointed manager of the Yangibana
    UJV, with Hastings retaining a 40% participating interest;
    the remaining Exchangeable Notes were redeemed and cancelled on completion, with consideration for the
    disposal measured at a fair value of $115,896,204;
    Hastings made the agreed cash payment of $7,363,068 to Wyloo following completion;
   each participant is required to fund its respective share of joint venture expenditure and the parties are to work
    together in relation to project financing;
   Wyloo has an option to acquire an additional 10% participating interest from Hastings at the lower of fair market
    value and $20 million; and
    Hastings' participating interest is subject to dilution if it does not meet its funding obligations under the Joint
    Venture Agreement.

On completion, the assets and liabilities previously classified as held for sale were derecognised. The carrying amount
of the disposal group was $116,079,909 and the Group recognised a loss on disposal of $183,705.

The Group retained a 40% participating interest in the Yangibana Project, which is accounted for as a joint operation in
accordance with AASB 11 Joint Arrangements. From the completion date, the Group recognises its share of the assets,
liabilities, revenues and expenses of the Yangibana UJV on a line-by-line basis.

The joint venture participants also entered into a Deed of Cross Security under which each participant grants a first-
ranking security interest over its JV Share and related Joint Venture Property to the other participant and the Manager
as security for obligations under the Joint Venture Agreement. The security is continuing, applies to the relevant JV
assets subject to permitted encumbrances, and may be enforced in specified default circumstances.

The disposal group formed part of the Yangibana Project segment. There were no cumulative amounts recognised in
other comprehensive income relating to the disposal group.

Measurement and impairment

At 30 June 2025, the disposal group was measured at fair value less costs of disposal. Following recognition of the
impairment of the Yangibana Project cash-generating unit, 60% of the written-down assets and associated liabilities
were classified as held for sale. Refer to Note 15 for further information regarding the impairment assessment.

In accordance with AASB 136 Impairment of Assets, the Group assesses at each reporting date whether there is any
indication that an asset or cash-generating unit (CGU) may be impaired. Where an impairment indicator exists, the
recoverable amount is determined as the higher of value in use and fair value less costs of disposal.

At 30 June 2026, the Yangibana Project cash-generating unit comprised the exploration and evaluation expenditure,
plant and equipment and right-of-use assets attributable to the Group's retained 40% participating interest in the
Yangibana UJV.

Impairment recognised at 30 June 2025

At 30 June 2025, impairment indicators were identified as the Group's net assets exceeded its market capitalisation and
the commercial terms of the Wyloo transaction provided observable market evidence that the value of the Yangibana
Project was below its carrying amount.

The recoverable amount of the Yangibana Project CGU was determined using fair value less costs of disposal, based on
the implied value under the binding transaction with Wyloo. The transaction implied a value of $193,160,339 for 100%
of the Yangibana Project and, after deducting estimated costs of disposal, a recoverable amount of $190,262,934.

The fair value measurement was classified as Level 2 under the AASB 13 fair value hierarchy as it was based on
observable market evidence from a negotiated binding transaction rather than a quoted price in an active market. No
significant unobservable Level 3 inputs were applied in determining the recoverable amount.

At 30 June 2025, the carrying amount of the Yangibana Project CGU assessed against the recoverable amount was
$225,294,464. An impairment loss of $35,031,530 was recognised at 30 June 2025, in addition to the impairment loss
of $141,368,886 recognised at 31 December 2024. In total, an impairment loss of $176,400,417 was recognised in the
year.

Equator Loan Notes and Attaching Options

In October 2024, the Company entered into a $5 million unsecured Project Loan Notes facility with Equator Capital
Management Ltd to fund costs associated with the staged development of the Yangibana Project. The initial $5 million
subscription was drawn down on 31 October 2024.

The Loan Notes bear interest at 12% per annum, calculated daily on a 360-day year. Half of the interest is payable in
cash and half is capitalised through the issue of additional Loan Notes.

The Loan Notes mature on the earlier of:

    the date on which the Company receives proceeds from a capital raising of at least $50 million undertaken at or
   around the Yangibana Project final investment decision, where those proceeds are permitted to be used to repay
    the Loan Notes; and
   31 October 2029.

The Company may redeem the Loan Notes earlier, subject to the notice, pro-rata redemption and make-whole
requirements in the loan documents.

Equator Capital Management Ltd is a long-term shareholder of the Company. The Company’s Executive Chairman, Mr
Charles Lew, has a non-controlling interest in Equator.

   The 2023 LTI performance rights were subject to performance over the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December

      35% subject to completion of construction and commissioning of Stage 1 of the Yangibana Project in accordance with
        the Board-approved schedule. The Board could approve a revised baseline where delays arose from circumstances
        that could not reasonably have been foreseen or managed;
      35% subject to the first on-specification concentrate being placed on a truck in accordance with the Board-approved
        schedule;
      10% subject to ESG measures comprising implementation of a 40% renewable power strategy, local employment

         for a continuous six-month period leading up to 31 December 2025; and
      20% subject to establishing a mine-to-offtake-partner logistics solution covering trucking, shipping and permitting
       by the time of first concentrate on truck.

   The performance conditions were assessed following the end of the performance period. Rights that did not vest, or
    that were held by employees who ceased employment and were not otherwise permitted to retain their rights, lapsed.

    2024 LTI performance rights

   The 2024 LTI performance rights were subject to performance over the three-year period ending 31 December 2026.
   The conditions comprised:

      35% subject to Board approval by 31 December 2026 of a feasibility study for Stage 2 downstream processing or
        further expansion of the Yangibana Project;
      35% subject to growth in Ore Reserves from the baseline of 20.93 million tonnes, after depletion. No rights allocated
        to this condition vest if the baseline is maintained, 50% vest for growth of 1.5 million tonnes and 100% vest for
       growth of 5 million tonnes, with straight-line vesting between these thresholds;
      10% subject to maintaining an upper-quartile ESG rating from a reputable ratings firm for each of the three years;
       and
      20% subject to relative total shareholder return against the specified peer group. No rights allocated to this condition
        vest below the 50th percentile, 50% vest at the 50th percentile, vesting occurs on a straight-line basis between the
         50th and 75th percentiles, and 100% vest at or above the 75th percentile.

NOTE 28: EVENTS SUBSEQUENT TO REPORTING DATE

Updated Yangibana Definitive Feasibility Study

On 13 July 2026, the Company announced the results of an updated Definitive Feasibility Study for Stage 1 of the
Yangibana Rare Earths and Niobium Project, completed by Wyloo as manager of the Yangibana joint operation.

The updated study refreshed the Project’s development assumptions, capital and operating cost estimates and
development pathway. It reported estimated initial development capital of approximately $333.4 million, of which the
Group’s 40% participating share is approximately $133 million. The updated study provides a current technical and
economic basis for assessing funding alternatives and progressing the Project towards a Final Investment Decision.

Wyloo sale process

Following completion of the updated Definitive Feasibility Study, Wyloo commenced a formal process to sell its 60%
participating interest in the Yangibana joint operation. Wyloo continues to manage the joint operation while the
sale process is underway. At the date of this report, no binding agreement for the sale of Wyloo’s interest had been
announced and the Group continues to assess the implications of any change in joint venture ownership for the
development and funding of the Project.

Thailand hydrometallurgical processing plant

On 14 July 2026, the Company announced plans to increase the proposed production capacity of the Kabin Buri
hydrometallurgical rare earth processing plant to approximately 10,000 tonnes per annum of feedstock and 12,000
tonnes per annum of Mixed Rare Earth Chloride output.

The proposed expansion forms part of the planned development of the facility under the acquisition arrangements
entered into with Enuo Holdings Pte Ltd on 31 March 2026. The acquisition remained subject to completion of the
transaction arrangements, applicable approvals and satisfaction of the relevant conditions.

The acquisition of the processing plant has not yet completed as at the date of the signed financial report. For more
details on the acquisition, refer to Review of Operations on page 8.

Issue of ordinary shares

On 27 August 2026, the Company issued 3,863,889 fully paid ordinary shares at $0.27 per share to professional and
sophisticated investors, raising $1,043,250 before transaction costs. The proceeds are to be applied towards additional
working capital. The shares rank equally with the Company’s existing fully paid ordinary shares.

Other than the matters described above, no matter or circumstance has arisen since 30 June 2026 that has significantly
affected, or may significantly affect, the Group's operations, results or state of affairs in future financial years.
